featured_reviews.name: Subir Das
featured_reviews.review_text:
A wide variety of fairly fresh Bengali and local sea fish varieties and excellent cutting of the fish in traditional style makes it the go to shop for fish lovers in the Kandivali- Borivali area.
Also available are traditional Bengali versions of pulses, condiments and other typical food/ seasoning items such as Nolen Gur, Kashundi, Sattu, Chinese noodles, Muri, Chanachur, Ghee, Bori, Pachphoron, Yellow mustard seeds etc. Fresh cut chicken and processed frozen chicken items and eggs are also available at reasonable rates.
Seasonal fish like Illish, topshe etc are also available here

featured_reviews.name: Nabarun Dev
featured_reviews.review_text:
Variety of fresh water fishes are available but prices are very high. Same fish available in Borivali west market with much lower price also with same quality.
Also get seasoned vegetables from Kolkata, price is insane (Brinjal is Rs200/KG).

featured_reviews.review_text: Very good bengali fish available. We've been regularly going there from Mira road. Gur, achar, dal, spices etc available too. Seasonal veggies too are good, but expensive.

featured_reviews.review_text: Good quality fresh fish available here. In any case found rotten, they change the fish then and there only. featured_reviews.name: Muntakem Haque
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent place to buy fresh high quality fish. Most fresh water fishes are available here, along with few sea fishes. A must visit place for any Bong or similar fish-loving community. Apart from fish, this place also has spices, snacks and other stuff popular in Bengal.

name: Sadhana’s Traditional koli seafood
description: Mumbai's fisherwoman Sadhana Vinde, famously known as Sadhana tai, has been serving authentic Koli-style seafood since 2007 with her family in cities like Mumbai, Pune, and Nasik. Her newly opened seafood restaurant in Thakur Village offers a rare chance to taste authentic traditional Koli cuisine that is hard to find in other restaurants. Previously and today also our restaurant also know as Sadhanas Kitchen .

featured_reviews.name: Vinaya Pagdhare
featured_reviews.review_text: Beautiful ambience, delicious home-like food, and a friendly, joyful owner. A perfect place for a family lunch or get-together. The crab lollipop was awesome, the mutton was yummy and tender, and Solkadi is a must-try!

featured_reviews.name: Yashasvi Prasad
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have been visiting this place for my weekend dinners as I’am a hardcore seafood lover and a taste coming from Koli style food truck was heaven .

I have tried almost everything from Surmai kalvan to their pan fried fishes to chicken thali and mutton too .

The taste is very much homely and they make everything from scratch with freshness . Nothing is stale or bitter.

Another thing is that they strongly BELIVE in “Atithi Devi Bhava” which states guest is god . Everytime to go to this place Riva and Manoj kaka especially has treated me like a home member and not just a customer .

They have grown a lot because of their relationship building with customer and the great taste that they deliver in Thakur village .

In a week usually it’s twice or thrice that I pay visit to this place and it’s hands down .

I personally recommend this to all the seafood Koli style food lovers who are searching for pocket friendly and delicious maharashtrian meals .

Guys, it’s authentic .

Keep up the good work .

5 stars to everything

featured_reviews.name: Pradnya Rambade
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently stayed at Fisherman Village for a monsoon staycation, and it turned out to be a really refreshing and peaceful experience. The moment we entered the property, the entire place felt calm, scenic, and surrounded by nature. Since we visited during the rainy season, everything looked extra beautiful — lush greenery, cloudy weather, the peaceful lake view, and ducks swimming around made the atmosphere feel straight out of a nature retreat.

One of the best parts of the stay was the ambience. The property has a very relaxing vibe, perfect for taking a break from the city rush. Sitting near the lake with light rain and cool weather felt extremely soothing. The view throughout the property was beautiful, especially during the evenings and early mornings. If you enjoy nature, monsoon is definitely the best time to visit.❤️

The food was also very good. The meals were fresh, tasty, and comforting, which added a lot to the overall experience. The staff was polite and welcoming, and the stay overall felt smooth and comfortable.✨

What we loved most was how peaceful and well-maintained the place felt. Whether it was walking around the property, enjoying the lake view, or simply relaxing with family and friends, the entire experience was memorable.🫶🏼

Overall, it was a wonderful staycation experience with beautiful views, good food, and a calm atmosphere. We genuinely enjoyed our stay and would definitely love to visit again, especially during the monsoon season. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a relaxing getaway near nature.👌

A special mention to one of the staff members who was extremely patient, polite, and helpful throughout our stay. They handled everything so calmly and made sure we were comfortable the entire time. Staff like that truly make a place memorable.

Fish served was fresh and very tasty.

Ac room was enough to hold a family get together for 20 people

featured_reviews.name: THE SIMPLE SOUL
featured_reviews.review_text:
Umm..nice Thali experience. We didn't have to wait for a table coz we got there early.
Space is very cramped though. Only 4 tables in the AC section, that too, 2 of them sharing a boundary with the washroom...ewww..not good for a dine out.
The thali is very basic. Rice, curry, bhakri/chapatis, sliced onion, whatever fried fish you order & dried prawns. 🍤🐟That's it. No solkadi, no desert, no salad. Nothing.
For the price, not VFM.

Only 1 boy to take orders from all tables + handle the Zomato/ Swiggy orders. He was rushed.
Yet, he was polite and courteous. Good going.

The gravy is extremely spicy 🔥🥵. Not for the faint-hearted. Had to forego half of it.
The fish is fresh, though.

Several patrons who asked for BOMBIL, were turned down bcz it wasn't available. Not great, since a seafood place ought to have these by default (one of the crowd favourites). Or ..perhaps ...being a Sunday, Tarri was trying to push the other costlier fish..who knows?? 🤔Anyways, the portion of fried prawns was decent.
No soft drinks available besides the bottled fizzies. The soft drinks were all warm & not chilled or cool post 12 noon. 🥤
And solkadi, which was just made, was not cooled before serving, post 1 p.m.
No desserts, except kharvas (decent) & caramel custard.🍮
Return if you want to sample other dishes, if not, would not recommend a second visit.

featured_reviews.name: Avik Roychoudhury
featured_reviews.review_text: 1 pack has 2 Mutton Pieces One Boiled Egg One Half Potato. Worst part is each Mutton Piece is 80% bone and 20% meat. The amount of attar is just revolting, I mean I know attar is part of Kolkata style biryani but the quantity they put is too much. We spent about 2k for 1kg mutton Biryani delivered at home for our guests and we were forced to eat such horrible food as there was no other option. They have the audacity to justify that they are right and are challenging me to send the left over food for verification. I am about to send the leftovers 2 pack hopefully it puts some sense into proper cooking.

featured_reviews.name: Jigar Raichada
featured_reviews.review_text: Very poor food quality. Egg roll tasted horrible and came with cucumber inside. Absolute mismatch of ingredients. Staff was rude and careless. Waste of money.

featured_reviews.name: Yash Raichada
featured_reviews.review_text: Poor food quality and worse taste. Egg roll had cucumber inside and tasted awful. Staff was rude and unskilled. Totally spoils the experience. Not worth the money.

featured_reviews.name: Soumik Biswas
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had ordered for a chicken biryani,  however received a chicken curry.

Definetely not even closest to what we get in Kolkata at the remotest area.

This is my 2nd order and a complete opposite experience from the last.

No consistency in quality.

Lastly there is no potato in there!

featured_reviews.name: Nirjhar Basu
featured_reviews.review_text: This is a typical bengali restaurant at thakur village, Kandivali, Mumbai. Foods are very good. Kolkata style biriyani is available here. Fish Kabiraji is another great dish. Mutton biriyani and veg items are also available here. Foods are priced at mid budget. Other than bengali food, barbeque and chinese items are also available.

featured_reviews.name: Meena Chillore
featured_reviews.review_text: The food is tasteless the rates of dishes are high he thinks about his about his own profit so please do not come here
